newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares barely lower on election worry.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares barely lower on election worry.

text.p: Istanbul shares lost all of the earlier gains in afternoon selling on Monday after deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said Islamist PM Necmettin Erbakan would resign in the next couple of days to hand power over to her in the run-up to snap polls, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,582, down one point, or 0.06 percent from Friday after brushing a high of 1,614 in early morning trade. It had dived 5.2 percent last week on political concerns.
Trade volume fell sharply to 12.10 trillion lira ($83.2 million) from Friday's 17.16 trillion ($118.7 million).
"In the next one or two days, the 54th government will come to an end, Erbakan will resign. In such an environment, the thing to do is to form an election government," Ciller told a meeting.
Brokers said the index rebounded slightly on support after dipping to a low of 1,577 on Ciller's words.
A RP spokesman from Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party (RP) later said they had conditionally agreed to hand over power to their pro-Western coalition ally True Path Party (DYP) later this week.
"The index has firm support at 1,570 levels. But prices will be squeezed in narrow ranges until the political picture becomes clear," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.

Ciller and Erbakan had announced on June 1 that they would seek early elections with a caretaker government to be headed by Ciller to overcome a row between the government and the secularist army over religious activism.
However, the coalition now has 274 seats in the 550-member parliament and relies on support from a small rightist party to pass an alteration in government and an early election law.
